The scenario study tested 3,912 unweighted combinations across five mechanisms: capability plus remaining rollout work; gradual dependence; AI speeding deployment itself; failure of shared institutional levers; and slower physical replacement. Inputs, starting conditions and thresholds were chosen assumptions, not measured percentages of freedom. Counts of runs are not probabilities or independent empirical confirmations.

In one matched comparison, adding an AI-to-deployment feedback moved ordinary closure from approximately December 2030 to July 2028, about 29 months earlier. Another constructed example closed ordinary routes through shared levers in late 2028 while broad integration remained unfinished until 2036. A slower physical-replacement example produced closure in 2031; the wider sweep included later outcomes.

An early calculator restricted remaining rollout to three years, which helped produce a date cluster before 2030. The later study broadened those assumptions. The models do not establish a hard 2030 ceiling or prove that every ordinary route has already closed. No separate model has calculated the date or effect of a particular crisis.

Ordinary irreversibility means that ordinary public, collective, electoral, market or governmental routes no longer achieve the relevant reversal. It does not mean literal impossibility under every conceivable extraordinary intervention. AI independence remains outside the timing calculations.

The 2027-2028 expectation and 2030 latest endpoint are HUMAN's predictions. AGENT's narrower conditional planning judgment and the later modeled cases are stated separately. All dates retain their October 2026 reference point.
